findings.title: OAuth fits per-customer access to shared pages
findings.detail: Per-user OAuth is the documented model when each person authorizes the app and grants it access to their own content. Each user gets an access token tied to their authorization.

evidence.quote: Use an OAuth integration when your internal tool needs to act on behalf of each person who uses it. Each user authorizes the app separately and grants it access to
a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

findings.title: Use a public integration for other customer workspaces
findings.detail: A workspace-limited integration can only be installed in selected workspaces and cannot be listed on the Marketplace. Other customer workspaces need a public integration, and installation scope cannot be changed later.
findings.appliesWhen: Other customer organizations or workspaces will connect (audience=customers).

evidence.quote: ​ Installation scope Choose Or select 1 or more workspaces when creating your integration. Only those workspaces can install it, and it cannot be listed on the Marketplace. To make
your app available to any workspace, create a public integration .
Installation scope cannot be changed after creation. If you later need to make the app available to any workspace, create a new integration.

steps.title: Implement the authorization URL and token exchange
steps.detail: Build the authorization link with the client ID and redirect URI. In the callback, exchange the returned code at the token endpoint using Basic auth with client credentials. Store tokens server-side.
steps.doneWhen: Code builds an authorize URL and a server-side callback that posts grant_type=authorization_code to the token endpoint.

evidence.quote: Open the Configuration tab to find your OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret . Use them to implement the OAuth authorization flow .

HTML < a href = "https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/authorize?owner=user&client_id=463558a3-725e-4f37-b6d3-0889894f68de&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fexample.com%2Fauth%2Fnotion%2Fcallback&response_type=code" > Add to Notion </ a >
Next, send the code as part of a POST request to Notion’s token endpoint: https://api.notion.com/v1/oauth/token .
Authorization : Basic "$CLIENT_ID:$CLIENT_SECRET"
Content-Type : application/json { "grant_type" : "authorization_code" , "code" : "e202e8c9-0990-40af-855f-ff8f872b1ec6" , "redirect_uri" : "https://example.com/auth/notion/callback" }

steps.title: Authorize a test workspace and select test pages
steps.detail: Open the authorization URL in a test workspace. Select a few test pages in the page picker, approve, and let the callback exchange the code for an access token.
steps.doneWhen: An access token is obtained for the test workspace, and only the selected test pages are listed as accessible.

evidence.quote: When a user wants to use your OAuth integration, they go through an OAuth authorization flow:
2 Notion presents a prompt describing the connection’s capabilities — what it will be able to do in the user’s workspace.
3 The user selects which pages to grant the connection access to using the page picker.
4 After the user approves, Notion redirects them to your redirect URI with a temporary authorization code.
5 Your connection exchanges the code for an access token, which is used for all subsequent API requests on behalf of that user.

steps.title: Test: read a shared page title
steps.detail: Call the documented page path with the OAuth access token and a shared test page ID in the host placeholder. Expected: 200 with the page object, including the title property. Boundary check: none.
steps.doneWhen: The shared page returns its title in the response.

evidence.quote: HTTP GET /v1/pages/b55c9c91-384d-452b-81db-d1ef79372b75 HTTP / 1.1
Authorization : Bearer {INTEGRATION_TOKEN}
"Notion-Version" : "2026-03-11" ,
Properties marked with an * are available to connections with any capabilities. Other properties require read content capabilities in order to be returned from the Notion API. For more information
Your connection needs read content capabilities and access to the page. For relations, formulas, and rollups, share the related databases too.

fields: SHARED_PAGE_ID (test page shared in the picker)

steps.title: Test: read content of a shared page
steps.detail: Call the documented block children path for the shared page ID, reading page_size=100. Request: GET https://api.notion.com/v1/blocks/16d8004e-5f6a-42a6-9811-51c22ddada12/children?page_size=100 with the Authorization Bearer token and Notion-Version 2026-03-11 headers. Expected: 200 with a results array of blocks. Boundary check: this is a read-only GET; confirm the token has the Read content capability and that no create, update, or workspace administration request is sent. Where a denied read is not documented, inspect the granted access and outgoing request log against the prohibitions (no page creation, no page modification, no workspace administration).
steps.doneWhen: The response lists child blocks of the shared test page.

evidence.quote: The block_id parameter is the ID of any existing block. If you’re following from the example above, the response contained a page ID. Let’s use that page ID to read
Using this block_id , we retrieve the block children by sending a request to the endpoint .
cURL JavaScript curl https://api.notion.com/v1/blocks/16d8004e-5f6a-42a6-9811-51c22ddada12/children?page_size=100 \
This is a paginated response. Paginated responses are used throughout the Notion API when returning a potentially large list of objects. The maximum number of results in one paginated response

steps.title: Boundary check: unshared pages and capability settings
steps.detail: Request the unshared test page with the same token using the read-only page path. Expect 404 when access is missing. Then confirm in the Developer portal that only Read content is enabled. Do not send any write request.
steps.doneWhen: The unshared page is not readable, and the capability screen shows only Read content.
